Since Arsenal won the Premier League Final in 2026, the team is looking to repeat in 2027. However, Liverpool and Manchester City are looking to claim victory for themselves too.

title: How Disneyland’s Cast Members Work Behind the Scenes to Create Magic for the Holidays: ‘Storytelling Is a Centerpiece to Everything We Do at the Company’
description:
In a 400,000 square-foot warehouse in Cerritos, Disney cast members create magic. 

	It’s the facility where cast members create decor for the park
body:
In a 400,000 square-foot warehouse in Cerritos, Disney cast members create magic. 

	It’s the facility where cast members create decor for the park — right now they are putting the finishing touches on Halloween and have already started winter holiday-scapes — fix everything from restaurant appliances to the iconic spinning teacups; it’s where signs get fresh coats of paint and carousel horses receive tender loving care. The facility houses machine shops, fabrication shops, a sewing team, a paint shop, and all kinds of skilled professionals who keep Disneyland beautiful and running efficiently. 
	

	And all the creativity and skill behind the decor and park enhancement is there to serve the storytelling. “Storytelling is a centerpiece to everything we do at the company, and particularly in how we approach our business. We always approach it story-first,” says 21-year veteran Phil Rahn, director, resort enhancement & horticulture. “Whatever we put in, whatever we design, whatever we create, there has got to be a reason for it.” 


	Tristen Tierney, associate project manager, resort enhancement (9 years at Disneyland), told his parents that he wanted to work at Disneyland when he was “11 or 12” and had already spent a couple years documenting the park’s decor, and deconstructing it to figure out what made it “elevated,” he tells Variety.  

	When he got a job at Disneyland, “I started buying the decor from property control”: cast members get to buy retired items at a deep discount. “I’d take it apart, really see how it was put together, and then I would rehab it myself. And I started creating a portfolio using the existing decor here at Disneyland.” Parks Enhancement noticed, and Tierney landed his dream job.  
	



	

	



	Tristen Tierney, associate project manager, resort enhancement, shows off a Halloween display headed for Disneyland in the park‘s giant Cerritos warehouse.


	The team was finishing up the decor for the Main Street USA Pumpkin Festival.

	The lamp posts on Main Street were set to be topped with the popular Mickey Mouse-shaped pumpkins backed with traditional fall foliage. Bunting will be attached using a clever slider system and secured with grommets to keep it in place. The pumpkins are fiberglass, a big improvement over the foam ones previously used. “They are lighter, and more robust,” Tierney says. 

	Everything is hand-carved, painted and sewn in the facility but craftspeople. 

	Every leaf, pumpkin, ribbon, paint and fabric must withstand the harsh Southern California sun and heat — the park officially unveils its Halloween decor Aug. 21 and on Nov. 1 it comes down. And those months are some of the hottest in the region. 

	“We have to easily be able to store the items here in the shop, be able to pull them down. We do a rehab on all our items, so every item goes through each decorator station,” Tierney says, adding that the team will make fixes and adjustments. “We don’t just put the put the thing back in the warehouse, forget about it, and put it back up. We need to make sure that it’s show ready and it’s safe. And this is just part of the checks we do for our over 8,000 pieces of individual pieces of decor.” 

	The enhancement team also experiments with installation techniques — the quicker the better as they must do their work after the park closes (sometimes that’s midnight) and before it opens at 7:30 a.m. And that team can be 12-15 people or more, depending on the size and scale of the projects, as Disneyland works with outside vendors to make sure that the decor is ready to go by opening time. “That provides a very small window for us to get in there. So, we have to be ready to go, and be able to install very quickly, and get back here within just a couple hours,” Tierney says. 




	

					Overall sign painter Devin Sweet repaints an original carousel horse at the Disney Cerritos warehouse.
	



	The seasonal decor’s themes and colors are developed with Walt Disney Imagineering and the Enhancement team.  

	The warehouse contains hundreds of boxes of florals and other small decor, all neatly and clearly labeled, rows of every textile used for umbrellas, chairs, bunting and other uses, rows of spare parts, props for the Main Street stores and other environments — an eye-popping inventory of everything large and small needed to keep the details of Disneyland’s attractions perfect. 

	There’s a giant teacup — stripped down to primer gray — in the spray paint bay waiting for its new coats. The machinists and fabricators are kept busy rehabbing the guts of cars from rides, making sure they are safe and can support the millions of guests each year. 
	

	The facility’s mechanics, machinists, metal workers and welders handle bigger projects involving vehicles from rides and other big display pieces. One of the ongoing tasks is to make sure rides are safe and in top working condition, like stripping down a Toy Story ride vehicle which needed some welded repairs and strengthening rods. 

	Devin Sweet, show overhaul sign painter and 20-year park vet, introduces the Show Overhaul sign shop, which is part of the Show Overhaul team. “We take care of the show elements that our guests personally interact with, so that would be attraction vehicles, outdoor vending carts and even trash cans. Some of the elements that maybe get overlooked in the park, but all tell the story of Disneyland,” she says. 




	

	



	Disneyland trash cans have fandom now, though. “Last year we had this great group of guests all dressed up as different Disneyland trash cans. It was fantastic,” she says. “But the great thing about these trash cans that’s maybe overlooked sometimes is that they have hand-painted elements on them.” The artisans stay true to the original colors and designs of the park — never deviating in 70 years.  And everything is hand-painted and hand-drafted with love — there are no computer terminals around and certainly no AI agents. 




	

					Devin Sweet talks about how her team handles repainting original carousel horses at the Disney Cerritos warehouse.
	



	“I think that’s always been a part of our story, right? So Walt Disney, when he first created Disneyland, he really wanted to bring his guests back in time. He wanted to bring them to a fantasy world,” says Devin tktkt. “So as soon as you step foot into Disneyland, you’re stepping into his childhood of Marcel, Missouri, at the turn of the 20th century, and so everything there had to be meticulously designed, and you wouldn’t have a computer-generated sign at the turn of the 20th century, right? So, it only makes sense that it’s done in the old-fashioned way.  And as artists, we’re so lucky that Disneyland really values that. Because this is a bygone art form, sign painting. And so, the fact that we get to do this and help bring that story to life, our guests notice.” 

	She was also working on refreshing a carousel horse called Lucifer’s Rose (all the carousel horses have names). She notes that the horses were bought by Disney in the 1950s from parks that were closing and are all hand-carved antiques — some even dating to 1875 — and each has a theme and color palette. “They’re solid wood, and so it’s our job to maintain these really special pieces of art. We follow artwork given to us by Walt Disney Imagineering, so that the horse looks exactly the same every time we do it.” 

	The gold on the horses is real as well. 




	

	



	“Our art is part of people’s memories and their stories,” she says. 




	

					Ting Ting Chiu, sign pictorial artist, paints a gingerbread figure at the Disney Cerritos warehouse.
	



	There’s another paint shop where artisans are getting Christmas holiday decor ready. Rahn says, “This is a group that we call Small but Mighty. There are seven pictorial artists on our team, but they cover all the resort and then all the interior black light painting for all the attractions.”He notes that former Disney topper Bob Iger just got a window on Main Street, “This is the team that made the window.” The shop’s proprietors’ names on Main Street all have a connection to Walt Disney and Disneyland, so it’s a great honor to get one.

	Inside the part of the tidy and ordered facility is a ribbon of corrugated metal decorated with large Disney characters. It’s actually the walls of the old machine, paint and other workshops at Disneyland. “So, when we moved over here, we wanted to take a little piece of that with us,” says Rahn. “So this is all hand-painted stuff that the artist did over the years.” 

	Tradition, memories and stories are what help drive the artisans. “Because we always have to keep up with the industry, and we need to make sure that we’re making wise business decisions while at the same time, we’re honoring the craft and we’re honoring the legacy of Disney, it all comes back to storytelling,” says Rahn. “So if you’re walking down Main Street and you see a sign for Carnation, and that’s a printed vinyl graphic, that’s not going to make sense. That’s going to take you out of the story that you’re in. So we have to make sure that the decisions we make are still honoring the tradition, but also the stories that we’re telling, and that really is what drives our decision-making. You know, there are places in the park where you can get away with printed vinyl signs, but we have to be really intentional with those decisions.” 




	

	






	

	






	

	






	

					Scott Carr, left, senior manager, manufacturing facilities, explains how his team has stripped down this Toy Story ride vehicle to make repairs and strengthen the chassis.
	



	Disneyland by the numbers: 

	Disneyland Resort is home to 36,000 cast members in hundreds of different roles. It’s Orange County’s largest employer. On average, full-time professional and skilled-labor cast members have worked at Disneyland Resort for more than 12 years.   75% of applicants surveyed cited career advancement as a top reason they wanted to work at Disneyland Resort.  




	

					A topiary-like Miguel from “Coco” is being readied at the Disneyland warehouse workshop in Cerritos for the park’s Dia de los Muertos celebration.
	






	

					The painters use detailed references when undertaking a project.
	






	

					Sign painter Adrian R. Sanchez works on a design for one of the Big Thunder mountain trains at the Disney Cerritos warehouse.

schema.headline: How Disneyland’s Cast Members Work Behind the Scenes to Create Magic for the Holidays: ‘Storytelling Is a Centerpiece to Everything We Do at the Company’

title: Amid ‘Spider-Man’ and ‘The Odyssey’ Leaks, Hollywood’s Battle Against Piracy Enters a Whole New Era
description:
What a slap in the face for Christopher Nolan.

	The Oscar winner and generation-defining talent spent three years writing, directing, producing and
body:
What a slap in the face for Christopher Nolan.

	The Oscar winner and generation-defining talent spent three years writing, directing, producing and editing “The Odyssey,” making his movie into its own kind of myth: a hand-crafted spectacle shot across six continents on the most rarefied cameras in the world, powered by the biggest stars and designed to be seen exclusively in movie theaters. But after only eight days of wide release last month, millions of viewers globally watched a pirated version of Matt Damon’s struggle to return to Ithaca on the social platform X. Audio and visual quality was as premium as the site could handle, and pixels on smartphones broadcast Nolan’s labor of love for free before it was yanked over copyright violation.
	

	This is the lawless new universe of piracy. In the ’90s, outlaws in the aisles filmed “Jurassic Park” on camcorders and sold copies on street corners. In the early aughts, “Finding Nemo” was burned onto blank DVDs and hustled all over major markets by the caseload. These were physical goods dealt in the shadows. Now, the moviegoing public can stumble on perfect replicas of theatrical blockbusters on numerous social apps and screen them in full before copyright teams can hit the panic button.


	The losses for media companies sit in the high tens of billions of dollars, a number that will climb as technology advances. This kind of piracy has become a double-edged sword for legacy media companies. To the delight of Hollywood, the “selfie generation,” Gen Z, has unexpectedly packed movie theaters lately — but they’ve brought along their digital habits. Audience members film crucial plot points and wild crowd reactions to show that they were there, and the studios look the other way and call it marketing.
	

	“It’s terrifying,” says Jonathan Eirich, the co-CEO of Rideback and producer of Disney live-action remakes “Lilo & Stitch” and “Aladdin.” Eirich wonders, “Do consumers understand how serious this is, or does it still feel harmless?”

	Just ask Peter Parker. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” fell victim to the same scheme as “The Odyssey” this summer. The gargantuan Sony Pictures hit is barreling toward becoming the highest-grossing movie ever in the U.S. It also played for 5.9 million X accounts — on opening day — before the studio shut down the bootleg version. Management consulting firm Kearney and anti-piracy company Muso estimate that piracy costs the industry $75 billion a year, and project it will reach $125 billion by 2028. With the average movie ticket costing $16, those 5.9 million views of “Brand New Day” on X surely cut into its potential revenue. In other words, Spidey himself can’t stop the astonishing speed with which illegal versions of brand-new tentpole films are appearing online. 



	

					Tom Holland in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day”
									Courtesy of Sony Pictures
	



	“Once a movie is out in the world, some piracy is inevitable,” one top film studio source says. “That’s the reality of releasing content globally in a digital environment.” 

	The current method for catching and killing pirated movies online is about as complicated as filling out customer service forms. Studios submit takedown requests to TikTok, Instagram and other social media companies and await responses. If the stolen files are replicated widely enough, alarmed phone calls are made and lawyers get involved, the source adds, and most platforms act swiftly (with the exception of Elon Musk’s “notoriously difficult” X, per the source). A spokesperson for X did not respond to a request for comment.

	The timing of this plundering couldn’t be worse. The industry is reveling in a rare moment of triumph as the summer box office hits $4 billion in ticket sales for only the second time since COVID closed theaters and cratered the economy (the 2026 total box office was more than $6.5 billion at press time). Titles like “Obsession,” “Backrooms,” “Toy Story 5” and “The Devil Wears Prada 2” — in addition to this summer’s smash hits “The Odyssey” and “Brand New Day” — have all contributed to this milestone. And all have been just as vulnerable to the near-instantaneous bootlegging. 
	

	Despite the streaming revolution and fierce competition from social media, gaming and YouTube, Hollywood largely makes money the way it always has. That means a film’s theatrical opening is gravely important for a studio — in terms of both recouping its investment and setting up a film for profitability in later release windows. Diminished ticket sales due to piracy also affect actors and producers, who negotiate profit participation as part of their compensation for mounting a movie or TV show. 

	“The Producers Guild and the MPA have their estimates on losses, but not knowing the specifics is almost more painful. It could be $5 million, $20 million or $50 million,” says Eirich. Most producers don’t  see a dime until break-even, he says, when a studio recoups the entire cost of its production budget. 

	Any harm to box office within this sensitive first window is a crisis. Audiences may be showing up in droves this summer, but moviegoing habits have yet to fully reach pre-pandemic levels. Internally at the studios, copyright divisions spend their energy targeting larger criminal operations enabling these digital pirates — the hives sharing and disseminating premium content. 

	“We build out the more complex cases against bigger piracy groups. We try to take them down and prevent them from reconstituting,” says Larissa Knapp, chief content protection officer at the Motion Picture Association. The trade group represents Hollywood’s interests in Washington, D.C., and has long crusaded to prevent billions in revenue from slipping through the cracks. Going after one rogue account showing “The Odyssey,” after all, is like picking cracked pepper out of a salad. 



	

					Jimmy Gonzales, Matt Damon and Himesh Patel in “The Odyssey”
									Melinda Sue Gordon/Universal Pictures
	



	Groups like the MPA still encounter piracy in the form of physical media. For example, the MPA routinely goes after rogue manufacturers of set-top boxes that help users pirate Netflix, Disney+ and other subscription media platforms. Policing that involves working with security departments at major companies like Amazon and Walmart to keep illegal goods off their commerce sites, where third parties are permitted to sell merchandise. 

	There are also still hustlers sitting at the movies with cameras. These days, the equipment is a bit more subtle. “They make pretty creative contraptions to conceal how they record. It’s not Kramer with the camcorder anymore,” Knapp says, referring to an episode of “Seinfeld” about movie piracy.  
	

	Another new threat is camera-enabled eyewear such as Meta AI glasses. Although the devices currently can record only three to five minutes of video, Knapp worries that criminals will be able to use AI to improve the quality of pirated recordings, smoothing out jerkiness or camera glitches. Who would spend their time capturing an entire movie on their glasses in three-minute blocks? Motive is a complicated question when it comes to piracy. 

	Dig long enough in any Reddit thread, and you’ll find Robin Hood figures who want to stick it to the ever-consolidating media conglomerates. Others have genuine accessibility issues, from those who don’t live close to movie theaters to superfans thwarted by rights deals that block their geographic locations from showing a movie or series. Regional culture also comes into play. Pirating “Heated Rivalry” in China is the only way to see it, given the country’s strict censoring of LGBTQ+ content and explicit depictions of sex. 

	While Hollywood adapts to these sophisticated new digital enemies, perhaps it is reconciling with the milder forms of piracy that they enable. For this year’s indie horror smash “Obsession,” TikTok was flooded with live reactions to the film’s many jump scares, and they’re still live on the platform. The same thing happened during a pivotal moment in 2025’s “A Minecraft Movie” when a beloved character from the titular game entered a scene, and Gen Z audiences went apeshit, screaming and cheering at AMC and Regal screenings around the world (and posting every second of their joy). The year before that, Cynthia Erivo’s rousing anthem “Defying Gravity,” which closed the first chapter of Universal’s “Wicked,” was clipped everywhere as fans wept in their reclining theater seats. 

	“Finding a full and perfect copy of a movie online will probably keep you from buying a ticket and seeing it in person,” Eirich says, weighing the complex calculus of how much piracy is too much. “But if the studio makes a decision that a little is OK? If it galvanizes people? Marketing is full of risk. The matter here is a lack of control. It’s when someone else makes that decision for you, it becomes a violation.”

schema.headline: Amid ‘Spider-Man’ and ‘The Odyssey’ Leaks, Hollywood’s Battle Against Piracy Enters a Whole New Era

title: ‘Saw V’ Director David Hackl Boards Action-Thriller ‘Solar Storm’ as Jack Hudson and Lorena Andrea Cast in Lead Roles (EXCLUSIVE)
description: David Hackl (“Saw V,” “Dangerous”) is set to direct the neo-noir action thriller “Solar Storm” for Pelican Pictures, from a script by Joe Rabl. Jack
body:
David Hackl (“Saw V,” “Dangerous”) is set to direct the neo-noir action thriller “Solar Storm” for Pelican Pictures, from a script by Joe Rabl. Jack Hudson (“The Devil’s Train”) stars and produces opposite Lorena Andrea (“Warrior Nun”).

	Unfolding over a single catastrophic day, “Solar Storm” follows Joe (Hudson), an ex-convict fighting to leave his past behind, whose path collides with Jasmine (Andrea), a woman desperate to escape a brutal marriage. When the largest solar storm in recorded history knocks out power, communications and order across the city, blackouts spiral into looting and riots. As the line between predator and prey burns away, the two go on the run through 24 hours of darkness — hunted by forces that may prove more dangerous than the storm overhead.
	

	“Joe is a man who’s done everything to leave his past behind, only to have the world itself collapse around him,” Hudson said. “The solar storm doesn’t just take the lights out — it strips people down to who they really are. David knows how to make that kind of tension relentless and cinematic. That’s the movie I wanted to make.”


	The cast also includes Massi Furlan (“Jumanji: The Next Level”), Valerie Huber (“Whiskey Cavalier”) and Werner Daehn (“The Lives of Others”) with additional casting underway on the remaining major roles.

	Producers include Hudson, Joe Rabl of Pelican Pictures and Walter Mair (“Liaison”) of Trigger Films, with Reinhard Besser (“The Ledge”) executive producing. Trigger Films is anchoring the financing, providing the U.K. tax credit and GAP financing. Mair will also compose the score.
	

	Behind the camera, the crew includes line producer Yanko Ushatov (“The Expendables”), stunt coordinator Rok Cvetkov (“Schindler’s List”), second unit director Alex Cvetkov (“SAS: Rogue Heroes”), aerial coordinator and helicopter stunt pilot Frédéric North (“Transformers: Dark of the Moon”) and animal coordinator Andrew Simpson (“Fallout”).

	“I wrote Solar Storm as a pure pressure cooker,” added Rabl. “One day. No power. No rules. Two people who need each other to survive. The storm outside is nothing compared to what’s happening inside these characters.”

	Principal photography is set to begin winter 2026 in Bulgaria on a budget of approximately €15 million.

	Hudson is represented by Framework Entertainment. Hackl is repped by IAG; Andrea by 42 and New Era Talent.

schema.headline: ‘Saw V’ Director David Hackl Boards Action-Thriller ‘Solar Storm’ as Jack Hudson and Lorena Andrea Cast in Lead Roles (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Disney Partners With Dhar Mann Studios, Which Has Been Given a 20-Episode Series Order
description: Disney has sealed a pact with Burbank-based content creator Dhar Mann Studios to create new youth- and family-oriented programming for its platforms
body:
Disney has sealed a pact with Burbank-based content creator Dhar Mann Studios to create new youth- and family-oriented programming for its platforms, the companies announced Friday. The deal kicks off with a 20-episode order on series produced by Dhar Mann Studios for Disney; further details were not revealed.

	“Dhar has built a distinctive voice and an enormous global following, with stories that are uniquely his own,” said Asad Ayaz, Chief Marketing and Brand Officer, The Walt Disney Company, and Debra OConnell, Chairman, Disney Entertainment Television, in a joint statement. “He and his team have forged an extraordinary connection with their audience, and we believe their optimistic, deeply relatable storytelling will connect in a meaningful way with Disney fans.”
	

	Dhar Mann Studios said that it attracts more than 170 million followers globally and nearly 300 million views each week across platforms, with programming that it describes as “uplifting, relatable stories rooted in universal experiences.”


	“For me, this is so much bigger than a content deal,” said Dhar Mann, founder of Dhar Mann Studios, in a statement. “I grew up with Disney stories. Now I get to experience that same magic through the eyes of my own family, and the idea that we now have the opportunity to create stories for Disney for the next generation is incredibly meaningful to me.”

	The companies said more details about the 20-episode order will be announced at a later time.

	Dhar Mann Studios is based in a three-stage, 125,000 square-foot production studio in Burbank, not far from The Walt Disney Co. headquarters. Dhar Mann Studios’ other partnerships include deals with brands like Adobe, the NFL and Gap. The company also produces original programming for Samsung TV Plus, where Dhar operates a FAST channel (which was the platform’s first creator-led original content deal) and a global vertical video slate with Fox Entertainment.
	

	“We’ve spent years building a direct relationship with our audiences and learning what makes them laugh, cry, share and, most importantly, feel seen,” Mann added in his statement. “Disney has spent generations creating stories and characters that become part of people’s lives. Bringing those two worlds together gives us an opportunity to dream much bigger about what these stories can become, where they can go and how many people they can impact.”

schema.headline: Disney Partners With Dhar Mann Studios, Which Has Been Given a 20-Episode Series Order

title: Trump’s White House Blasts Rosie O’Donnell After ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live’ Hosting Run: A ‘Nasty Woman’ and ‘Total Slob’
description: The White House has hit back at Rosie O’Donnell after she repeatedly skewered President Donald Trump during her guest-hosting gig on “Jimmy Kimmel L
body:
The White House has hit back at Rosie O’Donnell after she repeatedly skewered President Donald Trump during her guest-hosting gig on “Jimmy Kimmel Live” this week.

	In a statement to Entertainment Weekly on Friday, a White House spokesperson said: “Rosie O’Donnell is a nasty woman and a total slob whose brain has been completely destroyed by Trump Derangement Syndrome.”

	A rep for O’Donnell declined to comment on the White House’s statement. 
	

	Trump was the butt of many a joke during O’Donnell’s stint filling in for Kimmel, which ended on Thursday night. She began her first monologue on Monday with a bang: “If you thought the president hated ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’ when it was hosted by Jimmy Kimmel? Buckle up, people! Buckle up.”

	O’Donnell continued, “I’ve been living in Ireland for the past two years because of ‘Mango Mussolini.’ I read that Project 2025 and said, ‘Gotta get myself out of here!’ and I decided to go to Ireland where people are driven to drink regardless of who’s running their country.”

	During her final show on Thursday, O’Donnell signed off by thanking “everyone who’s been watching this week, especially the hungry, hungry hypocrite in the White House” (via The New York Times). She later performed a revised version of the classic Irish tune “Danny Boy,” calling it “Donny Boy” in dedication to Trump.

	“Poor Donny boy your polls, your polls are falling. Your reflecting pool is green as Mountain Dew. Your wig’s a mess, your ballroom is appalling, and with Iran you’ve bit off more than you can chew,” O’Donnell sang. “Measles are back, inflation is a-swelling; you post all night, you’re sleeping while you work. And what’s with all this useless crap you’re selling? Hey, sweetie pie, you’re driving us all berserk. But there’s a way to end this drama. It’s time to use that stable-genius brain. Since we all know you’ll never be Obama, why not resign, and make this country great again?”
	

	The comedian and the president have a longstanding beef, dating back to 2006, when O’Donnell mocked his bankruptcies while she was a moderator on “The View.” Ahead of taking the reins as guest host, O’Donnell spoke to Variety, revealing that she was “surprised” to receive the offer from Kimmel given what she called their “adversarial relationship.”

	“I support [Kimmel] in what he’s doing with the First Amendment, and our ability as entertainers and citizens to speak out against our government that’s enshrined in the Founding Fathers’ writings about our government, so I think he’s fantastic,” O’Donnell said. “And I wish that Stephen Colbert had the same kind of support when it happened to him, because he shouldn’t be gone either.”

schema.headline: Trump’s White House Blasts Rosie O’Donnell After ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live’ Hosting Run: A ‘Nasty Woman’ and ‘Total Slob’

title: Bonnaroo to Take Off 2027 to Recover From Extreme Weather
description:
Organizers for Bonnaroo Music and Arts Festival have announced that the festival will be taking a “much-needed” year off in 2027.

	The annual festi
body:
Organizers for Bonnaroo Music and Arts Festival have announced that the festival will be taking a “much-needed” year off in 2027.

	The annual festival, which takes place in Manchester, TN, has been plagued by severe weather over the past couple of years, leading to its cancelation in 2025 just a day after it started. In a post on its socials, Bonnaroo organizers explained that the extreme conditions are the root cause of needing to take a break in 2027 so that the campgrounds can recover.
	

	“As you know, we spent a great deal of effort and money working to improve the campgrounds and Centeroo in the months leading into the 2026 festival,” reads the post. “That included improved drainage, 4.5 miles of new roadways, and 135 acres of new grass, all which strengthened The Farm’s resiliency to Mother Nature. With limited time to recuperate from back to back years of storms, including the heavy rainstorm on Sunday this year, The Farm, particularly the main venue, needs a break to rest and recover.”


	Organizers said “this wasn’t an easy decision, and not one we take lightly, but in our hearts, we know this break will only make Bonnaroo better.”

	Bonnaroo has been canceled several times over the past few years, first in 2020 after it was pushed back due to the COVID-19 pandemic before inevitably being canceled. The following year, it was called off due to rainfall, and in 2025, Bonnaroo had a strong start on its first day before organizers ultimately canceled the rest of the festival due to weather.

	Bonnaroo 2026 took place from June 11-14, featuring headlining sets from the Strokes, Noah Kahan, Kehsa, Role Model and more.

schema.headline: Bonnaroo to Take Off 2027 to Recover From Extreme Weather

title: Seth Rogen, Colman Domingo, Danny Boyle Join Speakers Lineup at Toronto Market Summit
description:
The Toronto Intl. Film Festival’s Market, which runs Sept. 10-16, has added Seth Rogen, Colman Domingo and Danny Boyle to its list of speakers.

	Th
body:
The Toronto Intl. Film Festival’s Market, which runs Sept. 10-16, has added Seth Rogen, Colman Domingo and Danny Boyle to its list of speakers.

	The industry program, known as TIFF: The Market, has finalized its lineup and schedule of its conference program, the Summit, which has more than 70 sessions.

	Rogen and Boyle join The Visionaries strand, which features moderated conversations with “leading creators, executives and innovators forging unique paths in the global screen sector.”
	

	Rogen stars in two films at the festival: “Babies,” directed by Lauren Miller Rogen, and “Tangles,” an animated film that Rogen and Miller Rogen produced. Rogen will discuss these two films as well as his other projects, including “The Studio’s” upcoming Season 2.


	Boyle will reflect on his career and talk about his new feature, “Ink,” which opens Venice.

	Previously announced headliners include actor Gary Oldman, director Lee Chang-dong and producer Robbie Brenner.

	Another stand, Dialogues, features moderated conversations between writers, directors, screenwriters and producers that “focus on the nuances of their craft.” Speakers include Hirokazu Kore-eda (“Look Back”) and Yeon Sang-ho (“Train to Busan”). Other speakers include Kat Sandler, Rick Hansen, Amber Midthunder, Broderick Johnson, Brad Kane and Cody Lightning. Previously announced headliners are Pam Abdy, Mike De Luca, Curry Barker and Inde Navarrette.

	The Perspectives strand features moderated panel discussions on the state of the global screen industries. Speakers include Clint Bentley, Greg Kwedar and Domingo, as well as Roeg Sutherland and Glen Basner.
	

	Other speakers include Stephen Follows, Michael Dowse, Amanda Lebow, Moses Babatope and Nyla Innuksuk. The previously announced headliners are Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler.

	“Our aim was to reflect the big questions and opportunities facing the industry,” said Charles Tremblay, head of TIFF: The Market. “Giving delegates the diverse perspectives they need to navigate the shifting global dynamics was also a key part of our strategy; we’re thrilled to see how well it’s all come together.”

title: Netflix Sets Theatrical and Streaming Dates for Peter Berg’s World War II Drama ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Peter Berg is bringing one of World War II’s most improbable true stories to the big screen, and now it has a date.

	“The Mosquito Bowl,” directed
body:
Peter Berg is bringing one of World War II’s most improbable true stories to the big screen, and now it has a date.

	“The Mosquito Bowl,” directed by Berg (“Lone Survivor,” “Deepwater Horizon”), will open in U.S. theaters Oct. 30 before making its Netflix premiere Nov. 25, Variety can exclusively reveal, along with a first look image. The film will play in select AMC theaters during its theatrical run, along with additional locations across the country. It’s one of the few Netflix and AMC notable partnerships that has occurred, and the first since the release of the animated juggernaut “KPop Demon Hunters.”
	

	Based on the instant New York Times bestseller “The Mosquito Bowl: A Game of Life and Death in World War II” by Pulitzer Prize winner Buzz Bissinger, the film follows four of America’s top college football stars who set their fame aside to enlist in the Marines following the attack on Pearl Harbor. As they prepare for the brutal invasion of Okinawa, they play in a legendary game featuring some of the greatest players in college football history — a contest that, for many, would be the last they ever played. Berg produces through his Film 44 banner alongside Brian Grazer of Imagine Entertainment and Alex Gayner, with Ezra Emanuel, Bissinger and Jeb Brody serving as executive producers.


	Nicholas Galitzine leads the ensemble as John McLaughry, with Bill Skarsgård as Bob Baumann, Ray Nicholson as Tony Butkovich and Tom Francis as David Schreiner. Berg and Mark L. Smith (“The Revenant,” “Twisters”) wrote the screenplay. 

	Berg also makes an appearance on-screen as Gen. Buckner, heading a deep supporting cast that includes Brent Comer, Dominic Bogart, Jack Ingram, Ella Newton, Lola Bond, Stacy Clausen and Billy Smith. The film’s USO interludes feature Blake Erickson as Bob Hope, Claudia Ware as Frances Langford and Steven Sammut as Jerry Colonna, while sports personality Pat McAfee appears as a drill instructor.
	

	The artisans team includes cinematographer Jacques Jouffret; editors Jon Otazua and Garret Donnelly as editors; Rachel Tenner as casting director; and nine-time Academy Award-nominated sound designer Wylie Stateman, whose credits include “Lone Survivor,” “Once Upon a Time in…Hollywood” and “Inglourious Basterds.”

	“The Mosquito Bowl” also reunites Berg with his “Friday Night Lights” collaborators Bissinger and composers Explosions in the Sky. Their score gives the film its aching pulse.

	Berg has long been one of Hollywood’s most reliable chroniclers of American courage under fire, and “The Mosquito Bowl” arrives as awards season gets ready to heat up with the start of the fall festivals. Every cycle seems to produce a film that wants to speak directly to Middle America — the way “American Sniper” and “The Blind Side” once did. This one carries the same ambition.

	A moving drama that opens on a Herbert Hoover quote and builds toward the question: When is the moment a man changes during war? Think “Saving Private Ryan” by way of “Remember the Titans” — a film that wants audiences to confront sacrifice, masculinity and a disappearing piece of American culture on their way out of the theater. Nicholson and Francis are standouts, we hear, while Jouffret’s cinematography and Stateman’s sound design are said to be nothing short of invigorating. For all his box-office muscle, Berg remains an underrated filmmaker — a truth that “Deepwater Horizon,” “Lone Survivor” and “Patriots Day” have proved for years.

	The guy knows how to make a movie.

schema.headline: Netflix Sets Theatrical and Streaming Dates for Peter Berg’s World War II Drama ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Prehistoric Planet: Ice Age’ Soundtrack Features New Music by Composers Hans Zimmer, Kara Talve and Anže Rozman
description: The soundtrack for Apple TV’s “Prehistoric Planet: Ice Age” has been released, featuring music by Hans Zimmer and fellow composers Kara Talve and An
body:
The soundtrack for Apple TV’s “Prehistoric Planet: Ice Age” has been released, featuring music by Hans Zimmer and fellow composers Kara Talve and Anže Rozman.

	The score was written by Zimmer, Talve and Rozman of Bleeding Fingers Music and performed by the BBC National Orchestra of Wales. The trio are nominated in the Outstanding Music Composition For A Documentary/Nonfiction Or Reality Program (Original Dramatic Score) Emmy category. 
	

	For the series’ first two seasons, Zimmer, Talve and Rozman built an arsenal of custom instruments (Raptor Violin, HadroCello, Triceratone, FatRex) out of bones, fossils and dinosaur skull replicas, fusing them with a traditional ensemble to reflect the Mesozoic Era.


	To capture the Ice Age era, the trio used instruments including the Divje Babe flute, which was discovered in 1995 at the Divje Babe archeological site in Slovenia. It’s a bear femur with holes, thought be a Paleolithic instrument. “Our friend has a replica. We went into the caverns of the Postojna Cave [in Slovenia] and recorded it,” said Rozman. “It’s a very eerie sound that immediately transports the listener back in time.”

	For the score’s heavier and darker sound, the team removed high flutes, violins and brass. The composers also try to bring something unique to their scoring process. “We had a wall of cellos in a semicircle and double basses. We recorded an octobass, which is a huge double bass,” Rozman said.

	The instrument was so big that the player needed to stand on a stool to play it. Rozman said, “That gave us the rumbly, low feeling for the mammoths. The sounds of the terror bird (phorusrhacids) was based on a prototype, which was modeled on the larynx of an extinct terror bird species. But they took it to the next level, and the Triceratone was born, a wind instrument that created the guttural sound needed for the bird.
	

	For the rumbling weight of woolly mammoths, they utilized an Octobass; a massive 12-foot double bass generating subsonic 16 Hz frequencies. Paired with a low-register orchestra, it created an ancient, earth-shaking sonic mass.

	“We have always approached ‘Prehistoric Planet’ by asking how we can create sounds that feel like they’re transporting the listener back in time” said Zimmer, Talve and Rozman. “For ‘Ice Age,’ we built the score around a darker, more orchestral palette and continued experimenting with custom and ancient instruments to give the creatures and landscapes their own musical identity.” 

	The album continues a long-running collaboration between the three composers. Talve and Rozman; both composers at the Zimmer-founded collective Bleeding Fingers Music, have scored all three installments of ” Prehistoric Planet” alongside Zimmer.

	Currently, Zimmer, Talve and Rozman are writing the original score for HBO’s upcoming “Harry Potter” series.

schema.headline: ‘Prehistoric Planet: Ice Age’ Soundtrack Features New Music by Composers Hans Zimmer, Kara Talve and Anže Rozman

title: Hayden Panettiere's Ex Wladimir Klitschko Posts Tribute For Her 37th Birthday
description:
Hayden Panettiere's Ex
                          Emotional Tribute On Her Birthday
body:
Hayden Panettiere's Ex
                          Emotional Tribute On Her Birthday
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 21, 2026
                            8:43 AM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden Panettiere's ex-fiancé Wladimir Klitschko is celebrating her life on what would have been her 37th birthday.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            Wladimir, who is the father of Hayden's only child, Kaya, took to Instagram to memorialize Hayden alongside a throwback photo of Hayden grinning at the camera.
      
    
            He penned ... "Instead of celebrating the way we had planned, today we celebrate her life, her spirit, and the love she brought into this world."
      

            The former pro boxer went on to thank her fans, friends, and everyone who has reached out to him during this difficult time, adding ... "At a time filled with so much sadness, your kindness has reminded me that there is still so much good in humanity."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Wladimir then encouraged people to reach out to their loved ones and to always be kind, because "Love is a superpower."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            He finished his tribute by speaking directly to the late actress, saying ... "Happy Birthday, Hayden. ❤️ You are loved, you are missed, and you will never be forgotten."
      
    
            Wladimir originally spoke out about Hayden's death on Tuesday ... sharing a family selfie and vowing to never let their daughter forget her. He also celebrated her career, raving ... "She built an incredible career through immense talent, while also facing the darker sides of a very demanding industry. Nothing will erase the times we shared or the place she had in our lives."
      
    
                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            As we reported, Hayden died Sunday in South Carolina after a possible overdose. Medics were called to the apartment she was staying at with her boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, but she unfortunately could not be saved.
      
    
            Hayden's mom, Lesley Vogel, seemingly blamed Brian for her death in a statement she shared earlier this week, saying her daughter's death was "due to the involvement of a toxic individual who I believe led to her death."
      
    
            Meanwhile, Brian told TMZ, through a statement from his lawyer, Thursday ... "Hayden's death remains under investigation and it is important to allow that investigation to proceed. As has been publicly reported, police confirmed there were no signs of foul play. Out of respect for Hayden's loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time."

title: Natalie Harp's Intimate Letters to President Trump Revealed
description:
Natalie Harp's Letters To Trump
                          'You Are All That Matters To Me' ...
body:
Natalie Harp's Letters To Trump
                          'You Are All That Matters To Me' ...
                          'I Don’t Want To Ever Let You Down'
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 21, 2026
                            2:41 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 21, 2026
                                8:18 AM PDT
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Natalie Harp penned intimate letters to President Trump ... and now we're seeing them for the first time, and they show Harp's total devotion to Trump, telling him he's all that matters to her and she never wants to let him down. 
      
    
            Trump's executive assistant wrote the 2 alleged letters to the president during or after his May 2023 golf outing at his courses in Scotland and Ireland. The Daily Beast published the letters in full Thursday night.
      
    
            In one letter, Harp apologizes to Trump, believing she may have upset him during their overseas trip. She wrote that she thought she was the only person left behind at the airport the night before, so she panicked and called Trump while alone in a van at Customs without her passport. She said she should have just contacted the Secret Service.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Harp also wrote she was sorry for stepping onto the golf course instead of riding in a cart. She pleaded with Trump to "please forgive me" if she had done anything else to cause him trouble.
      
    
            She went on to write that she wants "things to always be right between us" and that she's "been distracted all week" while forgetting to eat and sleep at times.
      
    
            In addition, Harp wrote that she feared Trump had a lower opinion of her after other people made remarks about her, noting that she only wants to bring joy to Trump. She then ended the letter by referring to Trump as “my Guardian and Protector in this life.”
      
    
                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            In the second letter, Harp thanked Trump for getting her to “unplug” while they enjoyed their time together on the golf course. She wrote, “We could be out on the Course, with no machines, and even forget what time it was! I didn’t have to be 'Human Printer'" ... referring to her nickname in the White House because she quickly prints out favorable Trump articles and hands them to the president.
      
    
            Harp also wrote she could see that Trump noticed her occasional “slightly negative” mood because she's rapidly approaching burnout. She wrote that she envied anyone whose job "seems to be to talk with [Trump] and look pretty," insisting, "I want that job!!”
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            She also wrote that she feels like an "in-betweener" caught between Trump's staff and people who enjoy talking to him on the plane or at dinner. She said the experience harkens back to her days as a talk show host for the ultra-conservative "One America News Network," a job she says she hated.
      
    
            Harp wrapped up the second letter by telling Trump that he has the "absolute right to cuss me out, if need be, when I deserve it, because no one knows or cares about me more.”

schema.headline: Natalie Harp's Intimate Letters to President Trump Revealed
